change_summary: The journal retracted the paper, and an institutional investigation found the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. Those figures show accuracy by dose, which is the paper's main result (a 12% improvement at 200 mg), so the findings cannot be relied on. The authors have not responded.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] for the claim that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, and says this is why you chose a 200 mg dose. The paper reports that 12% result alongside Figures 2 to 4, and the retraction notice says the journal retracted the article, that the data in those figures had been fabricated and that the conclusions cannot be relied on. So the retraction touches your use of it in the Introduction. The impact on your draft is high, because your dose rationale rests mainly on this finding.
recommendation: The journal has retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] for the claim that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, and says this is why you chose a 200 mg dose. Remove or replace that citation and re-check the dose rationale it supports. Because your dose choice rests on it, raise the rationale with your co-authors or supervisor.
